highlights.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su proposed bringing back the Ryzen 7 5800X3D, set plan in motion before DDR5 shortages
highlights.description: AMD Director Travis Kirsch confirmed the rationale for relaunching the first X3D chip and explained why the company no longer offers many Ryzen 3 SKUs.

highlights.title: Instagram Launches Apple TV App With Reels and More
highlights.description: Instagram is now available on the Apple TV, bringing Reels, longer videos, and live shows via the platform to Apple's streaming device for the first time. The Instagram app for ‌Apple TV‌ lets users watch content from their favorite creators, discover videos, and resume watching across devices. Instagram describes the app as a way to watch together with friends and family, extending its video experience to the television. The app appears to have launched on October 23. highlights.title: OpenAI's isolated red-team agents built a hidden CPU cache channel to talk with no network or shared files
highlights.description: OpenAI’s red-team agents passed hidden messages through the CPU cache, a covert trick already shown to move data between cloud VMs.

highlights.title: SoftBank’s Son Plans $50 Billion Malaysia Tech Outlay, PM Says
highlights.description: Masayoshi Son of SoftBank Group Corp. chose locations in Malaysia for $50 billion in technology investments, the country’s prime minister said, an outlay that would accelerate the billionaire’s global bet on AI infrastructure.

highlights.title: Nvidia eyes converting old nuclear plants into massive AI data centers
highlights.description: Nvidia and PreussenElektra are studying whether decommissioned sites of German nuclear power plants can be repurposed as AI data centers, potentially cutting development time by reusing existing grid connections, land, and industrial infrastructure.

highlights.title: Apple's 'Servant' Copyright Lawsuit Win Upheld on Appeal
highlights.description: Apple and M. Night Shyamalan have won an appeal in the copyright dispute over Apple TV series "Servant," with a federal appeals court upholding last year's jury verdict in their favor (via Reuters). In its October 22 decision, the Ninth Circuit rejected filmmaker Francesca Gregorini's arguments that problems with the jury instructions and an unanswered question from jurors warranted overturning the result. sued in January 2020, alleging that the first three episodes of "Servant" copied her 2013

highlights.title: Cybersecurity bounty hunter says Samsung TVs use AI to record audio and screenshots for ads
highlights.description: A hacker reverse-engineered his own Samsung TV and found alarming spying activity, including code that used connected devices' microphones to listen to users.

highlights.title: Apple Wants to Fix Safari's Cramped Layout on iPhone Duo
highlights.description: Apple is considering changes to Safari on the iPhone Duo that would give websites access to more of the outer display, although the company has yet to settle on an approach. The challenge is allowing pages to occupy the area beneath Safari's side-mounted controls without making parts of a website inaccessible. In an Friday, October 23 WebKit post, Apple's Jen Simmons explained that an existing web setting could enable this, but Apple's research suggests many sites would not handle it correctly.

highlights.title: Chinese Manufacturer Dongshan Raises $1.3 Billion in HK Listing
highlights.description: Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co. a printed circuit board maker, raised about HK$9.9 billion ($1.3 billion) in Hong Kong’s biggest listing in nearly two months, which hit a volatile market for companies related to the artificial intelligence build out.

highlights.title: AI Provides ‘Zero Payoff’ to S&P 493 Outside Tech, Apollo Economist Says
highlights.description: Despite the significant investments ploughed into artificial intelligence it has provided “zero payoff” to corporate America outside of technology, according to Apollo Global Management Inc. Chief Economist Torsten Slok.
